subject: Follow-up: inference economics & reservation mechanics — next tests and asks
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: inference economics & reservation mechanics — next tests and asks

Hi Alex — thanks again for a productive demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before you loop in procurement: 

1) Goals you called out
- Predictable P95 and cost per inference for your patient-facing summarization pipeline
- Ability to scale to 600 concurrent requests during peak with <120ms median on 4k-token windows
- Controls for data residency and audit logging for a HITRUST scope down the line

2) Competitive framing we discussed (how Redwood differs from hyperscaler-managed GPUs)
- Dedicated pools with reservation guarantees (we can reserve a named pool for your org) vs ephemeral cloud instances that rely on spot/bursting — reduces tail latencies under load.
- Smart routing + fallback: we can route low-priority batch traffic to cheaper nodes and keep front-door capacity reserved for low-latency requests.
- Prefix/KV caching that materially reduces token cost for repeated clinical templates vs raw endpoint runs.

3) Proposed two-track validation tests (we recommend running both in parallel):
A) Reserved baseline: provision a small reserved pool equivalent to your target commit (e.g., 8 A100-equivalent GPUs) for a 2-week window. Run existing synthetic and real traces to measure P50/P95/P99, cold-start path, and cost per 1k tokens.
B) Hyperscaler parity: run the same traffic profile on the hyperscaler-managed endpoints (your existing vendor) with identical model configs to compare real-world variance and tail events.

We can provide the harness (bash + k6 scripts) and a CSV schema for results. Attached is a short benchmark matrix showing the metrics we suggest capturing (latency percentiles, tokens/sec, cost-model assumptions).

4) Procurement asks you mentioned
- Typical term length you prefer for reserved commitments
- SLA floor and credit mechanics for P95 and availability
- Data handling and audit options (KMS/HSM, log retention)

5) Next steps / dates
- You: share procurement contact + any internal compliance packet (you said procurement@acmehealth.com) — ideally today/mon morning.
- Us: provision a temporary reserved pool and share access to the harness by Tue EOD.
- Joint: run initial baseline tests Wed–Fri next week, sync Thurs to review preliminary deltas.

Attachments: redwood-temp-reservation-offer.pdf (pdf stub), inference-benchmark-matrix.csv (csv stub)

If that looks good I’ll kick off provisioning and loop in Karthik for the pricing/term sheet.

Best,
Grace
---
Grace O'Connor

Grace — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Procurement contact is included on this thread (procurement@acmehealth.com). They will need the term sheet and a brief summary of data handling controls.
- For the reserved baseline test, we prefer you mirror our production concurrency shape (bursty spikes every hour, sustained baseline ~200 req/s, peak 600). Can you confirm the harness supports variable traffic shapes and KV-cache warmup steps?
- On hyperscaler parity: we will run the same model on our cloud partner but need to understand any configuration differences (sequence length caps, quantization artifacts) that could bias results. Can you document the model variant names you expect to run?

Procurement: we have attached a short vendor questionnaire — please fill what you can and flag any items that need a Redwood legal or security contact.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference economics & reservation mechanics — next tests and asks

Alex / Procurement team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Short answers and operational plan below.

1) Harness & traffic shapes
- Yes: the harness supports time-varying traffic (we'll provide a parameterized k6 load file and a filler script to emulate your hourly spikes). We also include a KV warmup routine to bring prefix/cache hit rates to a realistic level.

2) Model variants to be tested
- redwood-open-4k-fp16 (baseline)
- redwood-open-4k-int8 (quantized path)
- redwood-llama-compat-4k (if you want an LLM-compat comparison)
Note: we’ll run identical tokenizer settings and sequence-length caps to reduce bias; any hyperscaler-specific model versions should be mapped to our closest equivalent — we’ll document the mapping in the test plan.

3) Temporary reservation mechanics and pricing
- We can provision a 2-week reserved pool (named to ACME trial) scoped to 8 GPU equivalents. Pricing for the trial is a pro-rated reservation fee; we can offer a 20% trial credit toward first-month committed spend if you sign a 12-month reservation within 30 days of the trial.
- SLA: P95 latency credit and availability credit tiers are in the term stub. We’ll send a formal term sheet to procurement (attached: redwood-temp-reservation-offer.pdf).

4) Security / procurement items
- Data residency: we support region pinning (us-west) and KMS-based key management.
- Audit logs: we can export request/response metadata (redacted if needed) to your SIEM.
- We’ll assign our security contact to fill the vendor questionnaire; Karthik / Sean are cc’d for pricing and commercial questions.

Operational timeline (concrete)
- Mon (today): procurement confirms any legal overrides and we send term sheet + DPA stub.
- Tue: infra team provisions reserved pool and we hand over access + harness.
- Wed–Fri: joint run; Thurs quick sync to review early delta.

Attachments included: redwood-temp-reservation-offer.pdf, inference-benchmark-matrix.csv

Grace
